bug_semantics: The authenticated GlassFish Administration Console uses JSFTemplating as its view-description/templating engine. JSFTemplating accepted and evaluated EL from console request processing with the ordinary Faces ELContext and no resolver in front of the standard resolver chain to reject dangerous reflective/static constructs. A crafted authenticated panel request could therefore reach static methods or constructors, getClass()/class traversal, and static fields; an attacker could reach Java process-execution facilities and run operating-system commands as the GlassFish service account. The closing component change installs RestrictedELResolver ahead of PageSessionResolver and rejects ELClass method invocation/constructors, getClass(), the class property, and (in the immediately following hardening commit) static fields.
flaw_origin: The unsafe EL design predates the available Git history. In eclipse-ee4j/glassfish-jsftemplating, blame of VariableResolver.java attributes the request-parameter datasource, method-expression creation, and general variable-resolution machinery to root commit 18d9b835fa98caec01ef026aab5ed907567dec0d, an 'Initial Contribution' importing 300 files and 141,910 lines whose source headers date the implementation to 2006. In eclipse-ee4j/glassfish, root commit 571714739b23e16c4c90d5229b806433920b3bcb is likewise an aggregate 'Initial Contribution' and already pins vulnerable jsftemplating 2.1.3. Neither aggregate is the smallest commit that originally wrote the flaw, and neither has a parent/history from which that commit can be decomposed.
ai_marker: Unavailable for the true BIC: the pre-import commit object that first created the unrestricted EL path is absent from public history. As boundary evidence only, `git cat-file -p 571714739b23e16c4c90d5229b806433920b3bcb` shows human author/committer Vinay Vishal and only `Signed-off-by: Vinay Vishal <vinay.vishal@oracle.com>`; the component root 18d9b835fa98caec01ef026aab5ed907567dec0d is authored by Jayasheelan Kumar and shows only `Signed-off-by: Jayasheelan Kumar <jayasheelan.kumar@oracle.com>`. Those aggregate import objects have no Co-Authored-By AI, Generated-with trailer, or bot identity, but protocol forbids substituting either import for the missing BIC.
evidence: Advisory bundle GHSA-96v6-hq43-x9h4/CVE-2026-2586 describes authenticated Administration Console RCE, declares org.glassfish.main.admingui:console-common < 8.0.2 fixed in 8.0.2 and org.glassfish.jsftemplating:jsftemplating < 4.2.0 fixed in 4.2.0. The first-party Eclipse disclosure at https://gitlab.eclipse.org/security/cve-assignment/-/issues/87 is titled 'Remote Code Execution via EL Injection', names CWE-94/CWE-917, and says crafted panel requests execute OS commands with the application service user's privileges.

At vulnerable component revision 6505f300ea51603c551c640da11e581a963e1825 (the 4.1.0 merge), https://github.com/eclipse-ee4j/glassfish-jsftemplating/blob/6505f300ea51603c551c640da11e581a963e1825/jsftemplating/src/main/java/com/sun/jsftemplating/el/VariableResolver.java shows resolveVariables dispatching attacker-controlled substitution content, RequestParameterDataSource returning ExternalContext.getRequestParameterMap().get(key), and MethodExpressionDataSource/MethodBindingDataSource calling ExpressionFactory.createMethodExpression on the supplied key. faces-config.xml at that revision contains PageSessionResolver but no restrictive resolver.

Direct component fix https://github.com/eclipse-ee4j/glassfish-jsftemplating/commit/c0eff55a82a96eeea9933104ae5003e9220dfb93 has parent 6505f300ea51603c551c640da11e581a963e1825 and adds RestrictedELResolver plus its faces-config registration. It blocks ELClass method/constructor invocation, getClass(), and class-property traversal. Follow-up 5f2daacc561e9a3a16b9b46ad462437f287dfd1b has parent c0eff55a82a96eeea9933104ae5003e9220dfb93 and also rejects static fields. GitHub's 4.1.0...4.2.0 comparison lists both commits; `git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/eclipse-ee4j/glassfish-jsftemplating.git` peels 4.1.0 to 2b1b95beea93f62d27c29c150645a364d0e01fb2 and 4.2.0 to 174e4659c0910ed6b084444d63aa5921dbe090c5.

In the assigned GlassFish clone, `git show cafaeae1b29b0552ca283e62004c047ea7082b34` shows the one-line product fix from jsftemplating.version 4.1.0 to 4.2.0, with parent ea54bc15d77b38d7b048ce7e9f6314eb5e4b9556. `git merge-base --is-ancestor cafae... 8.0.2` returns 0, while the same command against 8.0.1 returns 1; `git tag --contains cafae...` begins with 8.0.2. Direct tag reads of appserver/pom.xml yield 7.1.0=4.0.4, 7.1.1=4.0.5, 8.0.0=4.1.0, 8.0.1=4.1.0, and 8.0.2=4.2.0, reproducing the vulnerable/fixed boundary.

`git log --all -G'<jsftemplating.version>' -- appserver/pom.xml` traces the GlassFish dependency from root 571714739b23e16c4c90d5229b806433920b3bcb (2.1.3) through later vulnerable upgrades to cafaeae1b29b0552ca283e62004c047ea7082b34 (4.2.0). `git cat-file -p 571714...` has no parent header, and `git show --stat 571714... -- appserver/pom.xml` identifies a 984-line root import rather than an original flaw-writing change.

The component blame page https://github.com/eclipse-ee4j/glassfish-jsftemplating/blame/master/jsftemplating/src/main/java/com/sun/jsftemplating/el/VariableResolver.java assigns the core implementation to 18d9b835fa98caec01ef026aab5ed907567dec0d. Its commit page records 'Initial Contribution', 300 files, +141,910/-0, and no parent, while the file copyright says 2006. This directly demonstrates that the vulnerable implementation existed before the repository boundary and that the import cannot be accepted as the smallest BIC. Searches of the target history with both `git log -G'<jsftemplating.version>'` and `git log -S'jsftemplating.version'` find dependency/import history, not the missing pre-2018 source commit.

BIC-only AI assessment cannot be performed because the true BIC object is outside the preserved public history. The two inspectable root aggregate commit objects contain human identities and Signed-off-by trailers only; no AI trailer or bot identity is present, but those observations are explicitly not promoted to a NOT_AI finding because neither root aggregate is a valid BIC under the audit protocol.
reasoning: The vulnerability and its closing boundary are reproducible: the component's unrestricted Faces EL resolution made authenticated request-driven expressions capable of reflective/static process-execution access; c0eff55a82a96eeea9933104ae5003e9220dfb93 introduced the restrictive resolver, 5f2daacc561e9a3a16b9b46ad462437f287dfd1b completed static-field blocking, component 4.2.0 contains the series, and GlassFish cafaeae1b29b0552ca283e62004c047ea7082b34 first consumes 4.2.0 in product release 8.0.2. Causality cannot be carried back to a smallest BIC, however. Both the target product history and the component history begin with large root imports already containing/using the vulnerable implementation; the component's own 2006 copyright predates its 2018 root. Treating either root import as the introducer would violate the protocol's explicit ban on moves/squash aggregates. Consequently introducer and parent are null, parent absence is false, AI attribution cannot be judged from a true BIC object, and the correct closed status is BLOCKED rather than NOT_AI or an AI verdict.
remaining_gap: Genuine public-history boundary: obtain the pre-2018 Oracle/Sun JSFTemplating source-control history (including the original commit objects and parent chain for VariableResolver/general Faces EL evaluation) to identify the smallest flaw-writing commit, directly verify its parent lacks the unsafe EL path, and inspect only that BIC object's author/committer/trailers for AI evidence. The public GitHub roots are aggregate imports and cannot supply those facts.
